summary.intent: Fix bokeh/bokeh#9129: after a user picks a date, DatePicker shows the day before for browsers east of UTC. The change adds an offset correction to `_unlocal_date` and new Selenium integration tests.
summary.issue_fit: Partial. The issue's symptom is fixed for UTC+ users: a selected `toDateString()` value now round-trips to the same day. But the same correction now shifts every Python-supplied `value`, `min_date` and `max_date` back one day for users west of UTC, which moves the off-by-one bug to the other hemisphere.
summary.coverage: Read both changed files in full, plus the Python `DatePicker` model, the `Date` property transform, `convert_datetime_type` serialization and the git history of `_unlocal_date`. Reproduced the base and head `_unlocal_date` bodies under node in seven timezones. Uncommitted changes in the clone (an untracked `.mcp.json`) are outside this range and were not reviewed.
check_details: Reviewer ran a scratch node script under the work directory. It copies the base and head `_unlocal_date` bodies verbatim and runs them in seven timezones at head 36549bc (exit 0). For a UTC-midnight timestamp of 2019-09-20, the head returns Thu Sep 19 in America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York and Pacific/Honolulu, where the base returns Fri Sep 20. For 'Mon Sep 16 2019', the head fixes the base's Sun Sep 15 result in Europe/Paris, Europe/London and Asia/Tokyo.

The new Selenium integration tests in `tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py` were not executed: the run policy makes Selenium, a browser and the project build unavailable. What they can detect was settled by code trace instead.

findings.title: Stop shifting UTC-midnight timestamps back a day west of UTC
findings.trigger: A DatePicker gets `value`, `min_date` or `max_date` from Python, which serializes a `date` as a UTC-midnight millisecond timestamp. The page is then opened in a browser with a negative UTC offset, such as America/Los_Angeles.
findings.impact: `_unlocal_date` now subtracts `getTimezoneOffset()` before it reads the UTC ISO date. That moves UTC midnight into the previous UTC day, so `date(2019, 9, 20)` first shows and highlights as Thu Sep 19 2019, and the min/max bounds move a day earlier. The base showed these correctly, so users across the Americas get a new off-by-one display.
findings.change: Only the local-midnight strings written by `_on_select` (`toDateString()`) need the offset correction. Build the Pikaday date from `getUTCFullYear()/getUTCMonth()/getUTCDate()` for numeric timestamps, and from the local components for those strings. Don't mutate the argument with `setTime`.
findings.source: Regression against the base behaviour of `_unlocal_date`, which the base comment states as "the date comes in as a UTC timestamp".

findings.title: Make the DatePicker tests able to catch timezone regressions
findings.trigger: The new integration tests run on a host whose timezone is UTC (`.travis.yml` sets no TZ for `GROUP=integration`), and no test asserts the initially displayed date.
findings.impact: In UTC the base and head `_unlocal_date` give identical results for both input forms. So `test_js_on_change_executes` passes without the fix, and none of the tests would detect the UTC- regression above. The contribution guide's call for regression tests is not met in practice.
findings.change: Assert the input's initial displayed value (e.g. 'Fri Sep 20 2019') as well as the post-selection value, and run the browser under at least one positive and one negative UTC offset, for example by parametrizing a TZ override or the browser's timezone.
findings.source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md at base: "**DO** include regression tests when fixing bugs."

requirements.evidence: The displayed value after a manual selection now matches the selected day in UTC+ zones: in the node trace, 'Mon Sep 16 2019' gives Mon Sep 16 in Europe/Paris, Europe/London and Asia/Tokyo at head, where the base gave Sun Sep 15.

The fix for UTC+ users holds for the selection path (bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:82-83). The regression it introduces for UTC- users on the initial value is tracked as finding date_picker/unlocal-date-shifts-utc-timestamps-in-negative-offsets.

requirements.source: commit-4215c2d/"integration test for DatePicker displayed/selected dates"
requirements.evidence: The tests check the displayed value only after selection, and they run in UTC, where base and head agree (finding test_datepicker/tests-cannot-detect-timezone-regressions).
The checkbox is unchecked in the PR body, and the Selenium suite is unavailable in this run.
